subsystems.name: Strangelet seed
subsystems.role: a hypothetical droplet in which up, down and strange quarks sit in roughly equal numbers — the state that would have to exist before anything can be built with it.
parts: electron cloud that neutralises its charge

subsystems.name: Production driver
subsystems.role: the only known ways to squeeze nuclear matter hard enough to free quarks.
parts: heavy-ion collider (gold or lead nuclei at near light speed)

subsystems.name: Containment
subsystems.role: strange matter is denser than an atomic nucleus, so no ordinary vessel can hold it; only the strong force or gravity could.

subsystems.name: Conversion interface
subsystems.role: if strange matter is truly the ground state, its surface is where ordinary nuclei would be absorbed and converted.
parts: surface layer of partially deconfined quarks
weak-interaction step that turns down quarks into strange quarks

subsystems.name: Diagnostics
subsystems.role: detecting a droplet means looking for a rare, highly ionising particle with an unusual charge-to-mass ratio.

buildSteps.title: Compress nuclear matter
buildSteps.detail: Two heavy nuclei are collided at close to the speed of light, or a neutron star's gravity crushes its own core, until nucleons overlap and quarks can move freely.

buildSteps.title: Form a quark-gluon plasma
buildSteps.detail: Above a critical temperature or density, quarks and gluons become deconfined — a state already created in collider experiments.

buildSteps.title: Build up strangeness
buildSteps.detail: In the hot, dense fireball, collisions generate strange and anti-strange quark pairs; the droplet only survives if strange quarks outnumber anti-strange quarks.

buildSteps.title: Cool and condense
buildSteps.detail: As the fireball expands and cools, a region with the right density could condense into a droplet of strange quark matter rather than back into ordinary protons and neutrons.

buildSteps.title: Reach the stable ground state
buildSteps.detail: The droplet settles with roughly equal quark numbers and a slight positive charge, which binds electrons and keeps it electrically neutral overall.

buildSteps.title: Detect it
buildSteps.detail: A stable strangelet passing through a detector would show a distinctive charge and mass far outside the range of ordinary nuclei. None has been confirmed.

buildSteps.title: Convert ordinary matter (hypothetical)
buildSteps.detail: If strange matter is the true ground state, contact with ordinary nuclei would convert them, growing the strangelet — the property that makes 'engineering' with it so speculative.

buildSteps.title: Harness it (speculative)
buildSteps.detail: Turning the resulting energy release into useful work, or using the material as a structural component, requires physics and engineering that do not exist even on paper.

prerequisites.why: deconfined quark matter has been created in heavy-ion collisions, proving the state is reachable.
finding a rare strangelet requires enormous collision rates and dedicated detectors.

prerequisites.tech: Reliable equation of state for dense quark matter
prerequisites.why: it is still not settled whether strange quark matter is stable, metastable or not bound at all.
mass, radius and gravitational-wave data constrain whether quark matter exists in real star cores.
nothing can hold or steer a material denser than an atomic nucleus; no experiment has ever converted ordinary matter into it.

pathway.milestone: heavy-ion experiments and cosmic-ray searches set tighter limits on strangelet production
pathway.unlocks: either a confirmed detection, or stronger evidence that the state does not survive in practice.

pathway.milestone: improved dense-matter theory plus neutron-star observations (X-ray telescopes, gravitational-wave detectors)
pathway.unlocks: a firm answer on whether quark matter exists inside compact stars.

pathway.milestone: if stable strange matter is confirmed, dedicated searches in colliders and astrophysical data
pathway.unlocks: the first experimental handle on producing or finding the material.

pathway.milestone: theoretical control of the conversion process
pathway.unlocks: purely hypothetical applications — exotic structural materials, or engineered states of matter near compact stars. Proposed uses such as warp-drive components have no basis in known physics.
